context: Before rotation, the tree has 6 nodes. Root 1 has left child 0 and right child 4. Node 4 has left child 3 and right child 5. Node 5 has no left child and has right child 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. The variable node points to the unbalanced root 1, child points to its right child 4, and grand_child points to the left child of 4, node 3.

The balance factor is the height of the left subtree minus the height of the right. A leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree has height −1. A tree is balanced only if the absolute value of every node's balance factor is at most 1. The factors below follow from the connections in the figure.
Before rotation, root 1 has left subtree height 0 and right subtree height 2. Its balance factor is −2, so it needs a left rotation.
description: From left to right, the three panels show the tree before rotation, after the left rotation and grandchild transfer, and after removal of the dashed marks and adjustment of the layout.

The left rotation promotes child (node 4) to the root and demotes node (node 1) to the left child of 4. Node 1 takes the original left child position of 4, so grandchild 3 must move. Since 1 < 3 < 4, attaching 3 to the right of 1 preserves the strict binary search tree ordering: smaller on the left and larger on the right.
prose.result: After rotation, node 4 is the new root. Both its subtrees have height 1, so the whole tree is balanced. The inorder traversal of all 6 nodes remains [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6].

steps.announcement: Locate unbalanced root 1, its right child 4, and the grandchild to transfer, 3.
steps.explanation: Before rotation, root 1 has left child 0 and right child 4. Node 4 has left child 3 and right child 5, and 5 has only right child 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. Here node=1, child=4, and grand_child=3, with 6 nodes in all. The root's left and right subtree heights are 0 and 2, giving it balance factor −2. Save node 3, the left child of 4, before the left rotation so its reference is not overwritten.
steps.key_state: Initially, root 1 has left child 0 and right child 4. Node 4 has left child 3 and right child 5, and 5 has right child 6. The root has balance factor −2, and grandchild 3 is ready for transfer.
steps.title: Locate the unbalanced node and the grandchild to transfer

steps.announcement: Node 4 rises to become the root, node 1 becomes its left child, and grandchild 3 becomes the right child of 1.
steps.explanation: After rotation, root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5. Node 1 has left child 0 and right child 3, and 5 has only right child 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. Since 1<3<4, node 3 can move from the left of 4 to the right of 1. Dashed circles mark the old positions of 1 and 0. Dashed edges from the old position of 1 to the old position of 0 and to node 4 show the movement for comparison. There are still 6 nodes.
steps.key_state: After the left rotation, root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5. Node 1 has left child 0 and right child 3, and 5 has right child 6. Dashed marks show old positions for comparison.
steps.title: Rotate left and transfer grandchild 3

steps.announcement: Remove the dashed marks at the original positions and adjust the layout to show the rebalanced AVL tree.
steps.explanation: Remove the dashed marks at the old positions and adjust the layout. The connections stay the same: root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5, node 1 has left child 0 and right child 3, and 5 has only right child 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. There is no second rotation. Both subtrees of root 4 have height 1, so the whole tree is balanced.
steps.key_state: The dashed marks are gone. No second rotation takes place. Root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5, node 1 has left child 0 and right child 3, and 5 has right child 6. Both sides have height 1.
steps.title: Remove the dashed marks and adjust the layout

prose.summary: A left rotation promotes the right child of an unbalanced node and moves that child's original left child to the right of the demoted node. This restores balance and preserves the binary search tree ordering.
